text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Salah Boubnider, head of the national independent committee to supervise the elections, fails in a news conference on Monday to shed all the light on the watchdog's activities.
- "Terrorists" massacred 13 people in Merchiche village in the western province of Tlemcen on Sunday night. Among the victims were children and an elderly man. They were buried on Monday.
- Algeria is to appoint economists in its embassies in New York, Montreal, Paris, Brussels and 11 other foreign capitals in the country's efforts to attract foreign investors.

- Main workers' union instructed its branches to prepare for possible showdown with the government if the authorities fail to concede a salary hike. The Union Generale des Travailleurs Algeriens (UGTA) also threatens to stay away from three-way talks between union, business and government representatives over social issues.
